note: an unrecognized top-level field is a version we do not implement or an injection
reviewed: the parser REJECTS rather than stripping `extra` — silently dropping an unknown field would let a newer sender lose data and still be signed for

note: schema_version is a literal discriminator, not a range
reviewed: schema_version 2 is refused outright; there is no forward-compatible fallback to v1

note: no empty-string value is ever a valid brand
reviewed: the refusal is on EMPTINESS, not on length alone — no empty-string sentinel is ever a valid brand

note: a touched path that escapes the repo root
reviewed: a `..` segment is refused, never normalized away

note: unknown keys are refused at EVERY level, not only the top
reviewed: the unknown field is NESTED — the parser must recurse, not just check the top level

note: integers are safe and non-negative, checked before allocation
reviewed: the bound is integer AND non-negative, not merely `typeof value === number`

note: mode 120000 is refused everywhere in v0 (memo §12.3)
reviewed: mode 120000 is refused everywhere in v0 (memo §5.1), and the reason names the mode — the overlay manifest carries one valid rule so THIS is the rule that fires

note: the deny ruleset is broker-owned; its id is a literal the daemon cannot choose
reviewed: the deny ruleset id is broker-owned; a daemon-supplied id must never be honored — the manifest carries one valid rule so the literal check, not the empty-list check, is what refuses

note: the union is closed at four client/tool shapes
reviewed: an unsupported tool is refused, not degraded into a generic write

note: a Write carrying Edit's fields is not a Write
reviewed: a field that is valid on ANOTHER variant of the union is still unknown on this one

note: semantics_version pins how the operation is interpreted
reviewed: semantics_version is a literal, not a minimum

note: the daemon cannot know the environment digest before anything runs (memo §8.0)
reviewed: the daemon cannot know an env digest, so a claim carrying one is refused (memo §8.0, facts belong to the party that can know them)

note: nobody holds a resolved tree hash before the install runs — the asymmetry is the point
reviewed: the REQUEST side can never carry a tree hash — nobody holds one before the install runs

note: an empty git sha would compare equal to another empty one
reviewed: an empty string is not a head; the freshness check would otherwise compare disk against nothing

note: `projection` is declared only for the project phase; reported from fetch, one of the two fields is wrong
reviewed: the reason is legal and the phase is legal, but not TOGETHER — check REASON_PHASES is consulted, not just the two enums

note: binding_mismatch with no mismatch is a contradiction
reviewed: a binding-mismatch outcome with an empty mismatch list is unrepresentable — it would report a failure naming no field

note: an attestation with no verifier result is unrepresentable — the signature would attest nothing
reviewed: an attestation with no verifier result is unrepresentable — the signature would attest to nothing

note: an absolute file_path escapes the workspace the post-image set is defined over
reviewed: refused before projection, not confined after it — a path this shape must never reach the materializer

note: a `..` segment in a tool input escapes the workspace
reviewed: the rule the tree grammar applies to entries applies to tool inputs too — separate code paths, check both

note: raw_source_field is a closed set of runner payload keys
reviewed: the four accepted keys are the ones apply-patch-content.ts knows; a fifth would be an unaudited precedence rule

note: an unknown field inside a MultiEdit entry, two levels down
reviewed: the recursion reaches ARRAY ELEMENTS, not only nested objects

note: one path may appear at most once in touched_paths
reviewed: identity is byte-equality over the three fields, so a duplicate would make two encodings of one change compare unequal

note: a digest that is not 64 lowercase hex characters
reviewed: 63 characters is refused — check the bound is an exact width, not a minimum

note: touched_paths must be strictly ascending by UTF-8 bytes
reviewed: the refusal is on ORDER, not on content — the same two paths ascending are accepted, which is what makes the encoding canonical

note: sorted by UTF-16 code units, which a naive .sort() produces; UTF-8 orders the astral path LAST
reviewed: THE row that separates the two orderings — an implementation comparing with String#< instead of bytes accepts it

note: a MultiEdit with no edits changes nothing (no_edits) and must not reach admission
reviewed: the refusal is on the EMPTY list, not on the shape — the same record with one edit is accepted

note: an overlay manifest must name at least one include rule
reviewed: the canonicalizer and the wire parser now agree — an empty allowlist is a manifest that ships nothing and hashes as if it were meant

note: a gitwildmatch-v1 pattern with an out-of-order character class ([z-a])
reviewed: refused by the glob validator, not accepted as a bounded string — a pattern the matcher cannot compile must never reach selection

note: the same exact path twice is a duplicate rule
reviewed: the duplicate is measured on the exact path bytewise; the second copy is refused, not deduplicated

note: scratch/** and /scratch/** normalize to one rule, so listing both is a duplicate
reviewed: the duplicate is measured AFTER normalization — two spellings of one pattern are one rule

note: a wire manifest must arrive canonical: exact rules precede pattern rules
reviewed: the canonicalizer sorts this; the PARSER refuses it — the sender must canonicalize or its hash cannot match

note: exact rules must be in bytewise path order on the wire
reviewed: same canonicalizer caveat: accepted by the sorter, refused by the wire parser

note: a redundant leading '/' on a multi-segment pattern is not canonical spelling
reviewed: the sender must send scratch/**; the canonicalizer would normalize, the wire parser refuses

note: 1025 include rules exceed the canonicalizer's MAX_OVERLAY_INCLUDE_RULES (1024)
reviewed: the parser uses the same cap as the canonicalizer, not the 100000-entry content cap — the rules are canonical (sorted, unique), so the COUNT is the only thing that refuses

note: an uppercase-hex digest is not a lowercase 64-hex sha-256
reviewed: schema pattern AND parser both reject — this pins the digest pattern in the shared corpus

note: an overlay entry whose byte count is not an integer
reviewed: schema `type: integer` and the parser's safe-non-negative-integer check both reject 1.5

note: a fractional mirror version
reviewed: the integer half of the bound the negative-version row pins — 1.5 is refused by schema and parser alike

note: a persisted record whose created_at is not RFC3339-shaped (space instead of T)
reviewed: the shape rule — schema pattern and parser both reject; a stored record is decoded as strictly as a wire one

note: an RFC3339-shaped instant that does not exist on the calendar (February 30)
reviewed: schema ACCEPTS (the pattern is shape-only); the parser's calendar rule rejects — this row belongs to the pinned schema gap

note: an OpaqueId starting with '-'
reviewed: schema pattern and parser both reject — a leading dash would read as a flag anywhere the id reaches a command line

note: an OpaqueId containing a space
reviewed: schema pattern and parser both reject — the id grammar is URL-safe, and a space is never a byte of it
